correctness.rationale: For strictly positive rates, exponential racing makes the first failure independent of a mixture of exponentials for the next spacing; integrating an independent Laplace difference gives the exact rational nine-term Kendall tau formula. Sorting the normalized rates using a nonnegative three-gap parameterization, the deficit times the stated strictly positive denominator is a homogeneous degree-eight polynomial with exactly 40 positive integer coefficients; a self-contained exact symbolic checker from the delivered package recomputes and checks the identity. Two explicit positive monomials proportional to the squares of each adjacent rate gap force equality only when both gaps vanish. At a boundary with one vanishing rate and two equal active rates, tau is one third and normalized squared dispersion is one sixth, forcing the coefficient two fifths. The common increasing cumulative-hazard transform preserves Kendall tau; no unproved extrapolation to other n or other baselines.

originality.rationale: The main full-text comparison (Kochar 2022, Theorems 3.2–3.3) proves a qualitative stochastic-increasing order implying the uniform 2/5 concordance cap, but no exact positive rate-dispersion penalty and no sharp global coefficient 2/5. The 2005 homogeneous tau table does not vary hazards. Exchangeable TTE comparison and marginal-identifiability results do not imply this quantitative adjacent-order statement. A new exact rational identity and nonnegative polynomial certificate establish the stronger sharp claim. Full priority cannot be exhaustively certified.

value.rationale: The first two failure times for three competing independent risks are a basic natural reliability statistic; Kendall concordance quantifies dependence without dependence on a time-unit or common baseline. The previously established qualitative homogeneous upper bound lacks a quantitative heterogeneity modulus. The globally sharp, scale-invariant quadratic penalty indexed by normalized-rate variance supplies such a modulus, identifies the equal-hazard equality case and the two-active-component limiting obstruction; this is not an arbitrary numeric slice or routine consequence of the prior stochastic ordering.
